t.5.48.2: That king, his eyes copper-red with rage, spoke these weighty and meaningful words, suited to the occasion, to Prahasta, the best of ministers.
t.5.48.1: Gazing at that tawny-eyed one standing before him, the mighty-armed Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds wail, was seized by great fury.
t.5.48.3: Let this wicked one be questioned: where has he come from, and what is his reason? What is his purpose in destroying the grove and in threatening the rākṣasīs?
t.5.48.4: Having heard the words of Rāvaṇa, Prahasta spoke these words: "Take heart, may good fortune be yours; you need have no fear, O monkey."
t.5.48.5: If indeed you have been sent by Indra to the abode of Rāvaṇa, tell the truth; let there be no fear for you, O monkey, you will be set free.
t.5.48.6: If you are an envoy of Vaiśravaṇa, of Yama, or of Varuṇa, having assumed this charming form, sent by Yama or by Varuṇa…
t.5.48.7: Or are you a messenger sent by Viṣṇu, who longs for victory? For your energy is not that of a monkey; only your form is that of a monkey.
t.5.48.8: Tell me the truth now, O monkey, and then you will be set free; but if you speak falsehood, your life will be hard to preserve.
t.5.48.9: Or else, tell me the reason for which you have entered the abode of Rāvaṇa.
t.5.48.10: Thus addressed, the best of monkeys then said to the lord of the hosts of rākṣasas: "I am not of Śakra, of Yama, or of Varuṇa."
t.5.48.11: I have no friendship with Dhanada, nor have I been sent by Viṣṇu. This is truly my own nature: I am a vānara who has come here.
t.5.48.12: Since a sight of the lord of the rākṣasas was hard to obtain, I laid waste to this grove for the sake of seeing the king of the rākṣasas.
t.5.48.13: Then those mighty rākṣasas, eager for battle, arrived, and to protect my body I fought back against them in combat.
t.5.48.14: I cannot be bound by the nooses of weapons, not even by the gods and asuras; this boon too has come to me from the Grandsire himself.
t.5.48.16: Know me to be the messenger of Rāghava, whose might is boundless. And let these words of mine, which are for your good, be heard, O lord.
t.5.48.15: Wishing to see the king, I submitted to the weapon. I was freed by the weapon, but I have been sorely tormented by the rākṣasas.
